method: A frame is measured in 16x16 macroblocks: the width and height are each divided by 16 and rounded up, their product is the picture size in macroblocks, and that product times the frame rate is the macroblock rate. ITU-T H.264 Annex A states a level's limits as MaxFS (picture size in macroblocks), MaxMBPS (macroblocks per second), MaxDpbMbs (decoded picture buffer) and MaxBR (bitrate), and a stream conforms to a level when the picture fits MaxFS, neither side exceeds sqrt(8 x MaxFS), and the macroblock rate does not exceed MaxMBPS; the bitrate is limited to MaxBR multiplied by the profile's cpbBrNalFactor from Table A-2, which is 1.2 for Baseline, Main and Extended, 1.5 for High, 3.6 for High 10 and 4.8 for High 4:2:2 and High 4:4:4 Predictive. The tool walks Table A-1 from level 1 to 6.2 in order and returns the first level that satisfies all applicable constraints, so 1920x1080 at 30 fps is level 4 and at 60 fps is level 4.2. The reported DPB figure is MaxDpbMbs divided by the picture size, capped at 16 frames, which is how many reference frames a decoder at that level must hold; the reported maximum frame rate is MaxMBPS divided by the picture size, floored to two decimals so the figure is never above the limit. The binding line names the constraints that the level below fails, which is why the level was raised. Blank, non-numeric, exponent-notation, fractional-pixel and out-of-range values are refused with the failing field named, and an input combination that no level carries is refused with level 6.2's limits for the chosen profile rather than reported as a level. Level 1b is excluded because it only applies to constrained-baseline streams; VBV buffer size, the MinCR bitrate floor, interlaced field coding, slice and reference-frame signalling and the level-signalling syntax itself are not checked, and a level is a decoder capability label rather than a picture-quality setting. The tables assume frame-coded progressive pictures. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: ITU-T Recommendation H.264 (V15, 2024), Advanced video coding for generic audiovisual services, Annex A: Table A-1 levels with MaxFS, MaxMBPS, MaxDpbMbs and MaxBR, Table A-2 profile bitrate factors, and the A.3 constraint definitions including the sqrt(8 x MaxFS) side limits.
ISO/IEC 14496-10 (MPEG-4 Part 10) Advanced Video Coding, the jointly maintained text of the same level tables.
FFmpeg libavcodec/h264_levels.c, a published transcription of Table A-1 and Table A-2 with the same constraint checks, used to cross-check every level row and the profile factors.
